rationale: History: attempt-00 (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3,thr=256,sw=0)=195.8us; attempt-01 (M=16,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=8)=176.4us; attempt-02 reproduced attempt-00 exactly with sw=64 (195.8us), confirming swizzle is inert at M/block_M=1; attempt-03 (M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=64)=147.7us best. Key observed signals: DRAM is identical (33.8 MB) across all attempts including swizzle variants, so the panel-reuse proxy has NOT produced measured traffic gains at this shape -- hence down-weight traffic to 0.3 so it stops steering selection toward swizzle/tile choices that do not pay off. DRAM flatness also means block_N=64 already saturates reuse; keep N in {64,128,256} so solver may test wider N once, but launches weight stays 1.5 to favor N=256/128 if block count matters. block_K=32 lost repeatedly and is dropped; keep {64,128} to probe deeper K (attempt-01 already showed K=64 helps vs K=32, and larger K cuts pipeline iterations at fixed stages). block_M {16,32} only (M=32; 64/128 overshoot and did not win). Stages {2,3,4}: stage=4 still untested and now prioritized; stage=2 currently wins, stage=3 won at thr=256 earlier, so keep both. Thread domain changed to [128] as the early changed-thread hypothesis: attempt-03 did not use thr=128, and 64 never won, so we isolate 128 against the 256 winners to see if lower thread count with unpriced warp layout helps. Swizzle domain kept full [0,4,8,16,32,64] but traffic weight low so it does not dominate; if another swizzle variant reproduces flat DRAM/latency, we will further cut swizzle. Pipeline/footprint weights at 1 to penalize smem-heavy stage=4+K=128+N=256 tuples under the 32768 cap and hard portability cap. Next hypothesis: with traffic de-emphasized, test whether threads=128 with block_K=128/stage>=3, or block_N=128/256, beats the 147.7us K=64/st=2/thr=256 winner. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but does not execute the CUDA binary, so compile/memory status is a scoped estimate, not a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.
